claims.text: The baseline alloy has the composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The baseline alloy shows limited amorphous retention.
The baseline alloy has a complex or unstable thermal response during reheating.
The proposed intervention is an approximately 2 at.% boron addition.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will improve glass formation during rapid solidification.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will improve thermal stability during subsequent reheating.
The intervention should be effective at the high cooling rates achieved by rapid quenching.
The boron addition is not expected to prevent crystallization at extremely slow cooling rates.
Boron atoms are relatively small and chemically distinct in this alloy.
Boron increases local chemical and topological disorder and liquid-state frustration.
The increased disorder raises the nucleation barrier and disrupts crystalline-nucleus formation during solidification and heating.
The boron-modified alloy will retain a higher amorphous fraction after rapid quenching than the baseline alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will have a delayed crystallization-onset temperature during reheating relative to the baseline alloy.
The benefit may not manifest if reheating reaches too high a temperature or proceeds too rapidly.

contradictions.description: The stated success condition restricts reheating to below the crystallization-onset temperature, whereas the predicted delayed onset and the DSC falsification test require heating through crystallization onset. The intended reheating protocol is therefore internally unclear.
